mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past three months compresses equity discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy eases.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior three months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over the past three months signals labor market deterioration, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investor sentiment weakens.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC for UNRATE change is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad consumer demand weakness, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as corporate earnings face downward pressure.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a slowdown in industrial production (INDPRO) signals an impending economic deceleration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate investment plans are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances during late-cycle expansions when INDPRO declines, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) in the most recent quarter supports robust corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as economic momentum continues.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances with GDPC1 growth above 2.0%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When annualized inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.5%, it triggers expectations of tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as bond yields rise and equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, or the Rank IC for CPIAUCSL is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and corporate hiring weaken.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or the interaction Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-employment shock regime, a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals the initial phase of a labor market disruption, which is followed by aggressive monetary policy easing, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances during post-employment shock regimes when UNRATE rises, or the regime-specific Rank IC < 0.03.
